claims.title: The Magyar conquest (Honfoglalás)
claims.summary: Seven Magyar tribes under the chieftain Árpád crossed the Carpathians and seized the Carpathian Basin, founding the Árpád dynasty and the settlement that gave rise to the Hungarian state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-895-the-magyar-conquest-honfoglalas, claim TL:HUN:event:895:the-magyar-conquest-honfoglalas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pannonhalma Abbey founded
claims.summary: Benedictine monks settled at Pannonhalma, founding Hungary's first Christian monastery; it would help convert the Magyars, found the country's first school and, in 1055, produce the first document written in Hungarian.

sources.label: Millenary Benedictine Abbey of Pannonhalma and its Natural Environment

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-996-pannonhalma-abbey-founded, claim TL:HUN:event:996:pannonhalma-abbey-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Stephen I
claims.summary: Stephen, of the Árpád line, was crowned the first king of Hungary, traditionally with a crown from Pope Sylvester II, founding a Christian kingdom organised on Western models. He was later canonised as Saint Stephen.

sources.label: The Holy Crown of Hungary and the Coronation Regalia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1000-coronation-of-stephen-i, claim TL:HUN:event:1000:coronation-of-stephen-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol invasion and the Battle of Mohi
claims.summary: The Mongols under Batu Khan destroyed King Béla IV's army at the Sajó River and ravaged Hungary for a year, leaving much of the kingdom in ruins before withdrawing in 1242.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1241-mongol-invasion-and-the-battle-of-mohi, claim TL:HUN:event:1241:mongol-invasion-and-the-battle-of-mohi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Siege of Belgrade
claims.summary: Hungarian forces under John Hunyadi broke an Ottoman siege of Belgrade, checking the Turkish advance into central Europe for decades and becoming a celebrated victory of the medieval kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1456-siege-of-belgrade, claim TL:HUN:event:1456:siege-of-belgrade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Mohács
claims.summary: Süleyman the Magnificent destroyed the Hungarian army and killed King Louis II, ending the medieval kingdom and opening Hungary to Ottoman and Habsburg domination.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1526-battle-of-mohacs, claim TL:HUN:event:1526:battle-of-mohacs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman capture of Buda and the three-part division
claims.summary: The Ottomans seized Buda and Hungary fractured into Royal Hungary under the Habsburgs, Ottoman Hungary ruled from Buda, and the autonomous Principality of Transylvania.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1541-ottoman-capture-of-buda-and-the-three-part, claim TL:HUN:event:1541:ottoman-capture-of-buda-and-the-three-part, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reconquest of Buda
claims.summary: A Habsburg-led Christian coalition retook Buda from the Ottomans, part of the campaign that drove the Turks from Hungary after more than a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1686-reconquest-of-buda, claim TL:HUN:event:1686:reconquest-of-buda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Karlowitz
claims.summary: The Ottomans ceded almost all of Hungary to the Habsburgs, reuniting the country but binding it firmly within the Habsburg monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1699-treaty-of-karlowitz, claim TL:HUN:event:1699:treaty-of-karlowitz, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Revolution of 1848
claims.summary: A bloodless rising in Pest, with Sándor Petőfi among its voices, won the March Laws abolishing censorship and serfdom and establishing a responsible Hungarian government against Habsburg absolutism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1848-the-revolution-of-1848, claim TL:HUN:event:1848:the-revolution-of-1848, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Defeat of the war of independence
claims.summary: After Hungary proclaimed independence under Kossuth, the revolution was crushed by a combined Austrian and Russian army; the surrender brought executions and Kossuth's exile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1849-defeat-of-the-war-of-independence, claim TL:HUN:event:1849:defeat-of-the-war-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Austro-Hungarian Compromise (Ausgleich)
claims.summary: The Ausgleich transformed the empire into the Dual Monarchy, granting Hungary full internal autonomy with its own parliament while keeping defence and foreign affairs common to Austria-Hungary.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1867-austro-hungarian-compromise-ausgleich, claim TL:HUN:event:1867:austro-hungarian-compromise-ausgleich, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The founding of Budapest
claims.summary: Buda, Óbuda and Pest were unified into a single capital that grew into one of Europe's great cities; its historic core along the Danube is today a UNESCO World Heritage site.

sources.label: Budapest, including the Banks of the Danube, the Buda Castle Quarter and Andrássy Avenue

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1873-the-founding-of-budapest, claim TL:HUN:event:1873:the-founding-of-budapest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Collapse of Austria-Hungary
claims.summary: Defeat in the First World War destroyed the Dual Monarchy; amid revolution Hungary passed through a democratic republic and a brief communist regime before the conservative order of Regent Horthy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1918-collapse-of-austria-hungary, claim TL:HUN:event:1918:collapse-of-austria-hungary, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Treaty of Trianon
claims.summary: Hungary lost about two-thirds of its territory and population, leaving roughly three million ethnic Hungarians outside the new borders in Romania, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia and elsewhere; the trauma shaped Hungarian politics for a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1920-the-treaty-of-trianon, claim TL:HUN:event:1920:the-treaty-of-trianon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Vienna Award
claims.summary: Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy awarded Hungary parts of southern Slovakia from Czechoslovakia, the first of the revisionist gains that drew Hungary toward the Axis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1938-first-vienna-award, claim TL:HUN:event:1938:first-vienna-award, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Vienna Award
claims.summary: Germany and Italy awarded Hungary northern Transylvania from Romania, deepening Hungary's dependence on the Axis powers in its quest to reverse Trianon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1940-second-vienna-award, claim TL:HUN:event:1940:second-vienna-award, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hungary enters the war as an Axis ally
claims.summary: Seeking to keep and extend the lands restored by the Vienna Awards, Hungary joined Germany's war and took part in the invasion of the Soviet Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1941-hungary-enters-the-war-as-an-axis-ally, claim TL:HUN:event:1941:hungary-enters-the-war-as-an-axis-ally, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German occupation of Hungary
claims.summary: German forces occupied Hungary to keep it in the war and to deport its Jews, then the largest surviving Jewish community in Europe, numbering some 760,000 to 780,000 people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1944-german-occupation-of-hungary, claim TL:HUN:event:1944:german-occupation-of-hungary, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Deportation of the Hungarian Jews
claims.summary: Between 15 May and 9 July 1944 about 437,000 Jews were deported, mostly to Auschwitz-Birkenau, where some three-quarters were murdered on arrival; Horthy halted the trains on 7 July.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1944-deportation-of-the-hungarian-jews, claim TL:HUN:event:1944:deportation-of-the-hungarian-jews, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Arrow Cross seizure of power
claims.summary: After Horthy's attempt to leave the war, Germany installed the fascist Arrow Cross, which murdered thousands more Jews in Budapest before the Soviet conquest of the city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1944-the-arrow-cross-seizure-of-power, claim TL:HUN:event:1944:the-arrow-cross-seizure-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The siege of Budapest
claims.summary: The months-long battle for the capital between German-Hungarian and Soviet forces destroyed much of historic Budapest, including the castle and the Danube bridges, as the Red Army completed its conquest of Hungary.

sources.label: Budapest, including the Banks of the Danube, the Buda Castle Quarter and Andrássy Avenue

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1945-the-siege-of-budapest, claim TL:HUN:event:1945:the-siege-of-budapest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hungarian People's Republic
claims.summary: Backed by the Soviet Union, the communists seized total power and proclaimed a one-party People's Republic, imposing Stalinist terror, show trials and forced collectivisation under Mátyás Rákosi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1949-the-hungarian-people-s-republic, claim TL:HUN:event:1949:the-hungarian-people-s-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hungarian Revolution of 1956
claims.summary: A nationwide rising under premier Imre Nagy declared Hungary's withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact; the Soviet army crushed it on 4 November, killing some 2,500 Hungarians and driving about 200,000 into exile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1956-the-hungarian-revolution-of-1956, claim TL:HUN:event:1956:the-hungarian-revolution-of-1956, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: 'Goulash communism' and the New Economic Mechanism
claims.summary: János Kádár's reforms admitted limited market forces and private enterprise, giving Hungarians a relative prosperity and freedom unusual in the Soviet bloc.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1968-goulash-communism-and-the-new-economic-mechanism, claim TL:HUN:event:1968:goulash-communism-and-the-new-economic-mechanism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Pan-European Picnic and the opening of the border
claims.summary: A border gate opened near Sopron let some 700 East Germans flee west; Hungary's subsequent full opening of its frontier breached the Iron Curtain and helped bring down the Berlin Wall.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1989-the-pan-european-picnic-and-the-opening-of-the, claim TL:HUN:event:1989:the-pan-european-picnic-and-the-opening-of-the, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the republic
claims.summary: On the anniversary of the 1956 rising Hungary proclaimed itself a free republic, ending four decades of communist rule and beginning its transition to democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-1989-proclamation-of-the-republic, claim TL:HUN:event:1989:proclamation-of-the-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to NATO and the European Union
claims.summary: Having joined NATO on 12 March 1999, Hungary acceded to the European Union on 1 May 2004 in the bloc's largest single enlargement, completing its return to the West.

sources.label: EU enlargement: Hungary joined on 1 May 2004

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Hungary: From the Magyar conquest of the Carpathian Basin to a European republic, by way of Mohács and Trianon.", terralore.co/country/HUN/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-nato-and-the-european-union, claim TL:HUN:event:2004:accession-to-nato-and-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
